en.title: Bobrovsky chases Lundqvist while Toronto's goaltending debate grows
en.deck: One win lifts Sergei Bobrovsky past Henrik Lundqvist into sixth place on the all-time wins list, and makes him the winningest goalie born outside North America. He has been shaky at 3-5-2 with an .885 save percentage, and Utah beat Toronto 5-4 in October. The model likes the Mammoth a little more than the market does.
news: Jim Hiller confirmed Bobrovsky over Anthony Stolarz, who has a .910 save percentage, saying the goalie schedule was planned in advance.
Toronto shuffled its forwards: Easton Cowan is back with Auston Matthews, Dakota Joshua moves up beside William Nylander, and Gavin McKenna drops to the third line.
John Tavares practiced before the main group but stays out, week to week, with a lower-body injury from Oct. 15.
Utah: John Marino is on injured reserve, Kailer Yamamoto is day to day and Michael Carcone was activated. Karel Vejmelka is the likely starter after Sunday's 6-3 loss in Philadelphia.
records: Bobrovsky has 459 career wins, level with Lundqvist.
Mikhail Sergachev has eight points in a seven-game point streak, and Logan Cooley has six points in a three-game streak.
Scoring is the theme: 80% of Utah's games and 69% of Toronto's have gone over 5.5 goals, and the last seven meetings averaged 7.3 goals.
Vejmelka's .868 save percentage is well below expectation: the site's data has him 7.6 goals worse than expected this season.

sv.deck: En seger tar Sergei Bobrovsky förbi Henrik Lundqvist till sjätte plats i NHL:s all-time-liga för målvaktssegrar, och gör honom till den vinstrikaste målvakten född utanför Nordamerika. Formen är svajig med 3-5-2 och 88,5 i räddningsprocent, och Utah vann med 5-4 i det förra mötet i oktober. Modellen tror lite mer på Mammoth än vad marknaden gör.

John Tavares tränade före huvudgruppen men är fortsatt borta, vecka för vecka, med en underkroppsskada från den 15 oktober.

en.title: Nine straight losses and a coach under pressure: the Jets visit a hot Montreal
en.deck: Winnipeg is 0-7-2 in its slide, was shut out 7-0 in Carolina on Sunday, and coach Scott Arniel is being asked about his job. Montreal has won five straight and may get captain Nick Suzuki back. The market makes the Canadiens clear favourites, while the model is far less sure.

en.title: Two trade storms meet in Tampa, and Detroit plays on no rest
en.deck: Detroit has suspended Dylan Larkin after he refused to keep playing for the club, while Tampa Bay insists it will not trade Nikita Kucherov despite his reported request. On the ice, the Red Wings are 6-2-2 in their last 10 and the Lightning have won six straight at home. The market leans harder to Tampa than the model does.
news: Larkin was suspended without pay on Oct. 29. Interim GM Shawn Horcoff says Detroit is prepared to "wait as long as necessary" for the right return.

Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that Kucherov will not re-sign and wants a trade. GM Julien BriseBois answered that the club "unequivocally" has no intention of moving him, and Jon Cooper says Kucherov is fully part of the team.
Detroit won 5-3 in Florida on Monday with Daniil Tarasov in goal, so John Gibson is the likely starter here. Carter Mazur scored his first NHL goal.
Lightning: Yanni Gourde is out after hip surgery, Zemgus Girgensons is out and Erik Cernak is day to day.
records: Kucherov became Tampa Bay's all-time leading scorer on Oct. 24, passing Steven Stamkos.

sv.deck: Detroit har stängt av Dylan Larkin sedan han vägrat fortsätta spela för klubben, medan Tampa Bay försäkrar att man inte tänker trada Nikita Kucherov trots hans uppgivna önskemål. På isen står Red Wings på 6-2-2 de senaste tio och Lightning har vunnit sex raka hemma. Marknaden lutar mer åt Tampa än modellen gör.

en.title: Sullivan reshuffles as the Rangers try to end a four-game skid
en.deck: The Rangers have lost four straight, are 1-5-1 in their last seven and keep falling behind early. The Blues arrive on two wins, the last a wild rally in Detroit. The model and the market see nearly the same close game.
news: Mike Sullivan changed his lines: Pavel Dorofeyev moves up with Alexis Lafrenière and Mika Zibanejad, Gabe Perreault joins J.T. Miller, and Will Cuylle tries centre.

Blues: Colton Parayko is day to day and questionable. Torey Krug is out for the season, and Dillon Dube, Logan Mailloux and Tyler Tucker are also out.

Jimmy Snuggerud has five of his eight goals in his last six games, and the model flags his finishing as running hot.
The last six meetings averaged 5.2 goals, and Lafrenière's nine goals lead the Rangers.

en.title: The NHL's top scoring rate on no rest, against a Columbus attack in a slump
en.deck: Colorado scores 4.21 goals a game, most in the league, and won its third straight in Chicago on Monday. Columbus scored only once in Saturday's loss in Dallas and sits 29th in scoring. The market favours the Avalanche, but the model calls it a coin flip with Colorado playing back to back.
news: Colorado came back from 2-0 down to beat Chicago 5-2, with two goals each from Nazem Kadri and Jaden Schwartz. Mackenzie Blackwood played, and Scott Wedgewood is confirmed for this game.
Josh Manson is out with an ankle injury.
Columbus fell 3-1 in Dallas on Saturday to drop to 5-7-0. Rick Bowness says the team's best hockey is still ahead.
Jet Greaves is the likely Columbus starter, though not by a wide margin in the site's projection.
records: Artturi Lehkonen's nine-game point streak ended on Monday, after six goals in his last five games.
Nathan MacKinnon has eight points in his last five games, and Colorado's three-game winning streak is its best of the season.
Columbus's power play ranks 29th at 12.9%, and Zach Werenski is still looking for his first goal of the season.
Kent Johnson has been Columbus's bright spot, with three goals and seven points in five games.
betting: Market: Avalanche 1.79, Blue Jackets 2.07, about 54–46 without the margin. The model says 50–50, warmer on Columbus, partly because of the back-to-back and Wedgewood's .889 save percentage.

en.title: McDavid brings his 15-game opening point streak to Hellebuyck's home debut
en.deck: Connor McDavid has a point in all 15 Edmonton games, including an assist in each one, and 39 points in total. Connor Hellebuyck is expected to play his first home game for New Jersey after arriving in a trade on Oct. 23. The model and market agree almost exactly on the Devils as slight favourites.
news: Hellebuyck has won both Devils starts, allowing three goals on 39 shots. Sheldon Keefe says he has stepped right in.
McDavid became the fastest player to reach 30 assists, ahead of Wayne Gretzky's 1984-85 pace, and has 51 career points in 32 games against Hellebuyck.

Devils: Seamus Casey is out and Anthony Mantha is day to day.
records: McDavid's assist in all 15 games is the NHL's longest assist streak to open a season.
Edmonton is 7-0-0 on the road and scores 4.20 goals a game, second in the league.
Evan Bouchard has 26 points from the blue line, on a pace past Bobby Orr's defenseman record of 139.
New Jersey has won five of six and is 6-2-0 at home, and Jack Hughes leads the team with 16 points.

en.title: Kochetkov goes for 11-0 as the champions roll into Nashville
en.deck: Pyotr Kochetkov has won all 10 of his starts this season, a Hurricanes record for consecutive wins, and one more would match Jack Campbell's 11 from 2020-21. Carolina is 12-2-2 and comes off a 7-0 win over Winnipeg. Nashville has five losses after regulation, and the market and model agree on the Hurricanes.
news: Kochetkov made 26 saves against the Jets for his second shutout of the season. He is the third goalie to win each of his first 10 games of a season, after Campbell (11) and Carey Price (10).
Carolina is without Taylor Hall (upper body), Jordan Staal (calf) and Alexander Nikishin, who is out for a non-injury reason.

en.title: Eight days after a 6-5 thriller, the league's leakiest defence meets a Ducks attack on fire
en.deck: Vancouver won the first meeting 6-5 in overtime after trailing 5-2 late, but sits last in the NHL at 3-12-1. Anaheim has scored at least five in four straight and just beat Ottawa 6-3 with a Cutter Gauthier hat trick. Both the market and the model expect goals.
news: Gauthier's hat trick was part of a comeback from 3-0 down, with the last four Ducks goals on the power play.
